judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Dr Anita Sumanth, J.:— The mother of Prathap @ Giri, S/o Arul, has filed this petition challenging the order of detention dated 30-8-2025 under which said Prathap (detenu) has been detained at Central Prison, Salem. Several grounds are taken before us to assail the aforesaid order, the impugned order of detention.

2. We have heard Mr Vidhusan C. learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr R. Muniyapparaj, learned Additional Public Prosecutor assisted by Mr M. Sylvester John, learned counsel for the respondents.

3. The ground that appeals to us, is this. In the course of the detention order, the detaining authority expresses his apprehension that the detenu will be released on bail relying on the fact that one Harish Kumar had filed Crl.M.P. No. 5241 of 2023, and by an order dated 11-1-2024 had obtained bail before the learned Judicial Magistrate No. II, Hosur. Hence, the authority apprehends that that order would stand as a precedent for the detenu in obtaining bail. We do not agree as the facts and circumstances in the two cases are not comparable. The accused in that case had no adverse cases pending as against him whereas the detenu in the present case has 5 adverse cases against him.

4. That apart, the offence under that case was under Section 392 IPC relating to robbery whereas in the present case the charges as against the detenu are under Sections 303(2), 311 and 351(3) relating to theft, robbery and criminal intimidation, respectively, and are hence far graver in nature. The case of the detenu before us is thus is very different from the case of that accused. Hence, the subjective satisfaction on the basis of which the petitioner's son has been detained, is vitiated and the order of detention is liable to be set aside.

5. In light of the aforesaid discussion, this Habeas Corpus Petition is allowed and the Detention Order passed by the second respondent in S.C. No. 29/2025, dated 30-8-2025, is set aside.

6. The detenu viz. Prathap @ Giri S/o. Arul, aged 25 years, who is now confined in Central Prison, Salem, is directed to be set at liberty forthwith unless his presence is required in connection with any other case.
